title: Man. Post. Cap. IX: PLAC — Art. 10 'spoiled in his person' does not yield Adam's death imputed; more in Cap. XII
pass_a_gloss: Placeus asks whether Art. 10 really teaches the contrary. From 'spoiled of goods in Adam's person and fallen into misery' Garrigues infers dying by Adam's death imputed. Placeus denies the leap: those Confession words yield neither that conclusion nor any imputation of the gifts or the spoiling—fuller in Cap. XII.
pass_b_english: Does that tenth article of the Confession teach the contrary? Why then am I set against it? But it says we were spoiled of all those goods in his (Adam's) person, and fell into all this misery and curse. Therefore we die in Adam's own person—that is, by Adam's death imputed to us. No such thing follows from those words of the Confession. Indeed not even any imputation can be drawn from them, either of those gifts or of that spoiling—as will be shown more fully in chapter XII.
source_text: Contrariumne docet Art. ille Confessionis decimus? Cur igitur cum illo committo? At dicit nos in ipsius (Adami) persona spoliatos bonis illis omnibus, in omnem hanc miseriam & maledictionem incidisse. Ergo morimur in ipsa Adami persona, hoc est morte Adami nobis imputata. Nihil tale sequitur ex illis Confessionis verbis. Imo ne imputatio quidem ulla ex ijs colligi potest, vel donorum illorum, vel spoliationis illius, ut plenius declarabitur cap. XII.

choices.choice: Spoiling≠imputed Adam-death; no imputation from Conf; Cap XII
